nary_nodes.label: New Zealand passes English Language Bill
evidence: Lawmakers in New Zealand have passed a bill to make English one of the country’s official languages.
The bill — campaigned for by the nationalist New Zealand First party, part of the coalition government — passed its third reading in the House of Representatives on Thursday.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event representing the enactment or approval of legislation by a government
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org candidate captures legislative passage events. Minting LegislationPassage under Event as it represents government action on laws.

nary_nodes.label: Tamatha Paul condemns English Language Bill
evidence: In a video of a speech from that reading that has been viewed more than six million times on Instagram, Tamatha Paul, a member of New Zealand’s left-wing Green party, condemned the move as a waste of time, saying the “snowflake” government “see te reo Māori and they shiver in their boots.”

nary_nodes.label: Casey Costello defends English Language Bill
evidence: Casey Costello, a member of the New Zealand First party, was among those who defended the move in parliament during the third reading.
She said the purpose of the “short, straightforward bill” is to “recognize in legislation what has long been assumed in New Zealand. Namely, that English is an official language of our country.”

nary_nodes.label: Māori language revival campaign in the 1970s
evidence: The education system established by the colonial government aimed to assimilate Māori into the burgeoning new society by discouraging the use of the native language, leading to a widespread decline in its use. But a campaign by Māori to revive the language in the early 1970s led to the establishment of the first bilingual schools, and to te reo Māori being made an official language in the 1980s.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event representing efforts to restore the use and vitality of a language
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org candidate captures language revival campaigns. Minting LanguageRevival under Event as it represents organized efforts to revitalize languages.

nary_nodes.label: Justice Committee receives 1,601 submissions on English Language Bill
evidence: In a report presented to the House in June, the country’s Justice Committee said it received written submissions from 1,601 people and groups regarding the bill, and almost two-thirds of these opposed it.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event representing the collection of public input on proposed legislation or policies
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org candidate captures consultation events. Minting PublicConsultation under Event as it represents structured collection of public submissions on legislation.
